document.title: Action Plan as of 9/13/2001 7:55:51am
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret] Two days after 9/11, State creates an action plan documenting U.S. government activities so far and an immediate to-do list. It includes high-level meetings with Pakistani officials, including ISI Director Mahmoud Ahmed, and diplomatic approaches to Russia, Saudi Arabia, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Azerbaijan, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Georgia, Sudan, China and Indonesia.

events.description: UNSCR 1368 adopted, terming attack a threat to international peace and security.
US D and P met the Pakistanis, including ISID Director Mahmud.
WFP, UN and other organizations pulled out of Afghanistan.
POTUS meets Indonesian President Megawati; US-Russian Afghan Working Group meeting.
NAC authorizes Article V use if the attack is determined to be directed from abroad against US.
UNSCR 1368 adopted calling the attack a threat to international peace and security; UNGA adopts resolution condemning terrorism.
Prodi made statement for the EU condemning attacks and pledging cooperation.
US officials met Pakistanis including ISID Director Mahmud.
World Food Program, UN and other organizations pulled out of Afghanistan.
Embassy Islamabad double-tracks D message with GOP; cable to India/Bangladesh/Pakistan urging support.
USUN to approach Beijing on renewal/strengthening of UNSCR 1333.
POTUS and Indonesian President Megawati meet on CT cooperation; US-Russian Afghan Working Group meeting.
US/EU Ministerial on enhanced operational CT cooperation.
Meeting with Sudanese Foreign Minister Ismail in New York; cable to re-energize Six Plus Two.
State to press Tang Jiaxuan for public Chinese support.

key_claims: The US pursued coalition-building and Pakistani engagement, including with ISID Director Mahmud, on 12 Sep 2001.
US planned to seek renewed UNSCR 1333 targeting terrorist training camps in Afghanistan.
UN agencies and WFP withdrew from Afghanistan on 12 Sep 2001, prompting humanitarian aid planning.
The plan sought to re-energize Six Plus Two and engage Russia, China, and Central Asian states.
